appraisal_events.evidence: « Mais ils ne pensent rien du tout ; je leur ai dit que vous êtes sublime et ils sont beaucoup plus intimidés que vous. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup has publicly vouched for the narrator to his circle in superlative terms, so that the narrator arrives already elevated and the others are the intimidated party; the praise is undercut by the narrator's own parenthetical admission that his Balzacian pretext was pure bluff (« j'aurais été bien embarrassé de dire lesquelles ») and by his flattery of Saint-Loup in the same breath.

appraisal_events.evidence: « C'est que je vais vous dire, on m'a assuré qu'elle me croit tout à fait idiot. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage closes on the narrator himself reporting Mme de Guermantes's verdict that he is a complete idiot, a dismissal from the very person whose regard he is angling for through the photograph and the pretext of literary interest.

status_effects.explanation: Within Saint-Loup's military circle the narrator is locally raised: he has been announced as « sublime » and the others are more intimidated by him than he is by them.

The disclosed judgment of Mme de Guermantes, that he is « tout à fait idiot », lowers him at the point that matters most to him and exposes the borrowed, bluffing quality of the prestige he enjoys through Saint-Loup.
She gains local leverage without being present: her unfavorable opinion governs the narrator's anxious questioning, and both men treat her judgment as the standard worth worrying about.

ambiguities: The disparagement of the narrator is doubly mediated — attributed to Mme de Guermantes but reported by an unspecified « on » and relayed by the narrator himself — so its status as her actual verdict rather than hearsay is not settled by the text.

Saint-Loup's « vous êtes sublime » is sincere on his part, but read against the narrator's confessed fabrication it can be taken either as a straightforward elevation or as ironized praise; the reading chosen here treats the irony as real but not as cancelling the local social gain.
